The literal only thing that kept this game alive was the community and the humans in that community having the talent to create worlds and avatars. So here we are, a decade into development, with practically the exact same issues this game has always had still unfixed, and the developers of Vrchat decide that prioritizing AI is the best move. While this game is one of the biggest reasons I even got into VR, I cannot say I can recommend it.

Back in July 2022, the developers added Easy Anti Cheat to prevent malicious mods/clients that crashed and harassed other users. Despite this, crashing other users through particle-based methods and ripping avatars remain relatively easy, while EAC blocks any way for client side QOL or accessibility mods to be used. This is also why I dislike VRC+. Some functionality that was previously available through these client side mods, such as expanded avatar favorites through eg. FavCat, is now locked behind this subscription.

The developers also recently decided against adding any way to label AI generated content. I personally feel that users should be able to tell whether content was made using generative AI, especially those who would rather avoid it.

It's a shame to have to create this review, because I used to really like this game.

 Yes, it's free. Yes, it has lots of amazing moments as it's entirely built around the premise of socialization combined with immersion, leading to a everly evolving experience fuelled by it's active community. These factors are great, but there are some things that I wish are improved on.
 My main complaint, regulation - I'm chill with (prefer even) minimal boundaries in terms of rules and regulations on platforms. However, if we have moderation not actively taking measures against underage users to the extent of literal kids being in the same lobbies with porn avatars (and this is a thing I COMMONLY see), then the the very loose lines I've drawn have most certainly been crossed in terms of regulation. This furthermore results in the game's current child predation problem, as I have witnessed multple children getting groomed in-game. This is horrible and should have more action taken against it (excluding ID age verification as I'll explain later in this review). VRChat used to be the ultimate hub for human creativity, beautiful community-made worlds, and genuine social connection. Today, it is a textbook example of a company prioritizing corporate greed and investor demands over the safety, desires, and hard work of its own playerbase. 

If you are thinking about playing this game or buying VRChat+, [b]please read this first.[/b]

[h2]1. The Ultimate Betrayal of Creators (The 95% AI Slop Issue)[/h2]
VRChat was built on the backs of human artists, 3D modelers, and passionate creators. Recently, the platform has been flooded with low-effort, Generative-AI "slop" worlds and assets. 
The developers put out a survey asking the community how to handle this. [b]Over 21,000 people responded, and 95% asked for a label and a filter for AI content.[/b] 
The developers' response? They explicitly said [b]NO[/b]. 

Their reasoning? They stated that if they add an AI filter, [i]"filters get set once and forgotten, and then you never see that part of VRChat again."[/i] 
[b]THAT IS THE ENTIRE POINT OF A FILTER.[/b] We don't want to see stolen, soulless AI generation. The developers admitted they would rather protect the "feelings" of AI-prompters than protect the real artists who built this game. Furthermore, VRChat is currently violating Steam's TOS by failing to disclose their own use of AI on their store page.

[h2]2. Rampant Unmoderated Grooming & Predator Issues[/h2]
This game is absolutely not safe for children, and parents need to be warned. VRChat has a severe, well-documented issue with predators and groomers. Users have consistently reported finding adults actively grooming minors, and when reported, VRChat moderation does absolutely nothing. The predators simply make new accounts or are ignored entirely. 
[i]The developers currently fight harder to protect AI-generated slop than they do to protect minors on their platform.[/i]
